title: Ops signal sprint check — Console & Tooling
content:
Sprint checkpoint — ops signal (2026-10-05)
Owners: Aisha (notes), Ben, Lena, Ravi, Marta

Purpose: quick sync to align on rollout signals, recent aberrations in panel analytics, and short-term UI fixes that could impact telemetry. Focus on 24-72h signals and action items for the week.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (eng-console-tooling)
- Ben Chow (observability)
- Lena Martinez (frontend)
- Ravi Singh (rollouts)
- Marta Oliveira (data-analytics)
- Guests: Sam (SRE) for incident context

High-level status:
- Rollout: panel-circuit gating is at 60% of internal canary; no customer-facing errors yet, but increased p95 tokenization latency observed on one cluster.
- UI: accessibility pass for panel editor ~80% complete; dark-mode visual regression surfaced in Canary 2.
- Analytics: ingestion lag spike last night (approx 22:00 UTC) caused by a malformed event spike; pipeline backpressure mitigated by retry backoff change.

Observability signals (last 48h):
- Edge panel p50: 38ms (baseline 35ms)
- Edge panel p95: 210ms -> saw bump to 370ms between 03:00-04:30 UTC on cluster-stable-3
- Request error rate: steady at 0.02% (no SLO breach)
- Telemetry pipeline lag: median 2m -> spike to 45m for ~1.2k events at 22:13 UTC
- Cost per 1k requests (est): +3% week-over-week due to increased retries

Root-cause hypothesis:
- Early signal: single client producing high-frequency partial-update events that partially blocked the analytics write buffer. Backpressure bubbled to runtime via sync path used by the old metric flush.
- Contributing: a recent change in the panel editor (PR #4832) introduced extra sync points when autosave races with the submission flow; this is correlated with the malformed events.

Immediate actions taken (done):
- Marta patched ingestion consumer to drop malformed events and log client id (RDW-11504).
- Temporarily throttled write-consumers for cluster-stable-3 to reduce downstream backpressure (Sam).
- Rolled back autosave atomic-change introduced in PR #4832 on canary cohort 2 for safety (Ravi).

Open action items (owners + ETA):
1) Run a targeted repro of autosave race
   - Owner: Lena
   - Steps: create automated Selenium script to submit rapid partial edits + autosave; run against Canary-2 image.
   - ETA: 2026-10-07
2) Harden telemetry consumer to batch and validate with defensive schema (avoid blocking on single malformed event)
   - Owner: Marta + Ben
   - ETA: 2026-10-09 (scope MVP: drop/metric and alert on malformed > threshold)
3) Rework panel editor to async-flush autosave (remove sync path)
   - Owner: Lena, code PR: WIP (frontend/issue RDW-11688)
   - ETA: 2026-10-15 (aim to land behind feature flag)
4) Add a short-lived feature-flagged test that simulates high-frequency client events to the nightly regression suite
   - Owner: Ben
   - ETA: 2026-10-08
5) Postmortem draft and customer comms prep (if needed)
   - Owner: Aisha + Ravi
   - ETA: 2026-10-10

Metrics we will watch (dashboard cards):
- panel.tokenize.latency.p95 by cluster (alert threshold 300ms)
- telemetry.ingest.lag.99 (alert when > 30m sustained for 5m)
- autosave.error.rate (new metric)
- feature-flagged canary failure-rate by cohort

Discussion notes / fragments (raw):
- Lena: "I can repro locally with a simple script; looks like the autosave promise sometimes rejects and we swallow the error which then produces an empty payload - that explains malformed events."
- Ben: "We need a quick guard: if event schema invalid -> return 400 client side, and log client id for throttling decisions."
- Ravi: "Let's keep rollback until we have ingest guard. Canary cohort 1 is green; cohort 2 saw the hiccup only because of internal stress tests we ran last night."
- Sam: "SRE ran short-term throttling; removed after 45m when pipeline stabilized. We should automate throttling for backpressure signals."

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Keeping rollback longer protects customers but slows feature validation; cost of rollback: UX regression for a week, but lower risk to ingestion pipeline.
- Rapid autofix in runtime (drop events) hides client bug; prefer to fail fast + surface to client.

Decisions:
- Short-term: keep autosave change rolled back on canary-2 and add ingestion guard (MVP)
- Medium-term: re-architect autosave to be async and non-blocking; land behind FF and test with simulated noise

Parking lot / questions:
- Do we need automated throttling based on telemetry lag? (SRE + Observability sync)
- Should we add client-side event schema validation library to SDKs? (product question)

Next sync plan:
- Quick standup tomorrow 09:30 PT to review Lena's repro and ingestion guard PR status
- Full postmortem draft review next Tue 10/12 (Aisha owner)

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Draft incident timeline ASAP and capture related PRs in postmortem template (link above).
- Ping legal for potential customer notification template if ingestion lag impacted customer analytics exports.

Attachments / references:
- PRs: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/console/pull/4832 (autosave sync change)
- Jira: RDW-11688 (panel editor autosave rework), RDW-11504 (ingest guard), RDW-11721 (canary cohort metrics)
- Slack thread: CL4K2J9Q1 (panel-ops)

End notes: rough capture — will tidy for postmortem. Expect updates as PRs land.

-- Aisha
